section_summary.extract_value: This introduction discusses the prevalence of appearance-focused exercise goals, particularly for women in Western culture, and their association with negative body image. It introduces Self-Determination Theory (SDT) as a framework to understand these associations, differentiating between extrinsic and intrinsic goals and various forms of behavioral regulation (external, introjected, identified, intrinsic). The section highlights the potential role of introjected regulation, especially guilt-based motivation, in linking women's body image to appearance-related exercise goals, noting that previous research has not simultaneously considered all three constructs. No specific studies are presented in this section.
